In [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]], the '''asymmetric Laplace distribution (ALD)''' is a continuous [[probability distribution]] which is a generalization of the [[Laplace distribution]]. Just as the Laplace distribution consists of two  [[exponential distribution]]s of equal scale back-to-back about ''x''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''m'',  the asymmetric Laplace consists of two exponential distributions of unequal scale back to back about ''x''&nbsp;=&nbsp;''m'', adjusted to assure continuity and normalization. The difference of two variates [[Exponential distribution|exponentially distributed]] with different means and rate parameters will be distributed according to the ALD. When the two rate parameters are equal, the difference will be distributed according to the Laplace distribution.

==Characterization==

===Probability density function===

A [[random variable]] has an asymmetric Laplace(''m'', ''&lambda;'', ''&kappa;'') distribution if its [[probability density function]] is<ref name=KOZ2000>{{cite journal|title=A Multivariate and Asymmetric Generalization of Laplace Distribution|last1=Kozubowski |first1=Tomasz J. |last2=Podgorski |first2=Krzysztof |page=531|year=2000|journal=Computational Statistics|volume=15|issue=4 |doi=10.1007/PL00022717 |s2cid=124839639 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/256065510|access-date=2015-12-29}}</ref><ref name="JAM">{{cite journal |last1=Jammalamadaka |first1=S. Rao |last2=Kozubowski |first2=Tomasz J. |year=2004 |title=New Families of Wrapped Distributions for Modeling Skew Circular Data |journal=Communications in Statistics – Theory and Methods |volume=33 |issue=9 |pages=2059–2074 |url=http://www.pstat.ucsb.edu/faculty/jammalam/html/Some%20Publications/2004_WrappedSkewFamilies_Comm..pdf | doi=10.1081/STA-200026570|s2cid=17024930 |access-date=2011-06-13 }}</ref>

:<math>f(x;m,\lambda,\kappa)=\left(\frac{\lambda}{\kappa+1/\kappa}\right)\, e^{-(x-m)\lambda\, s \kappa^s}</math>

where ''s''=[[Sign function|sgn]]''(x-m)'', or alternatively:

:<math> f(x;m,\lambda,\kappa)  = \frac{\lambda}{\kappa+1/\kappa}
    \begin{cases}
      \exp \left( (\lambda/\kappa)(x-m) \right) & \text{if }x < m
      \\[4pt]
      \exp ( -\lambda\kappa(x-m) )  & \text{if }x \geq m
    \end{cases}
  </math>

Here, ''m'' is a [[location parameter]], ''&lambda;''&nbsp;>&nbsp;0 is a [[scale parameter]], and ''&kappa;'' is an [[asymmetry]] parameter. When ''&kappa;''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1, ''(x-m)s &kappa;<sup>s</sup>'' simplifies to ''|x-m|'' and the distribution simplifies to the [[Laplace distribution]].

===Cumulative distribution function===

The [[cumulative distribution function]] is given by:

:<math> F(x;m,\lambda,\kappa)  = 
    \begin{cases}
      \frac{\kappa^2}{1+\kappa^2}\exp ((\lambda/\kappa)(x-m)) & \text{if }x \leq m
      \\[4pt]
     1-\frac{1}{1+\kappa^2} \exp (-\lambda\kappa(x-m))  & \text{if }x > m
    \end{cases}
  </math>

===Characteristic function===

The ALD characteristic function is given by:

:<math>\varphi(t;m,\lambda,\kappa)=\frac{ e^{i m t}}{(1+\frac{i t \kappa}{\lambda}) (1-\frac{i t}{\kappa\lambda})}</math>

For ''m''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0, the ALD is a member of the family of [[geometric stable distribution]]s with ''&alpha;''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2. It follows that if <math>\varphi_1</math> and <math>\varphi_2</math> are two distinct ALD characteristic functions with ''m''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0, then

:<math>\varphi=\frac{1}{1/\varphi_1+1/\varphi_2-1}</math>

is also an ALD characteristic function with location parameter <math>m=0</math>. The new scale parameter ''&lambda;'' obeys

:<math>\frac{1}{\lambda^2}=\frac{1}{\lambda_1^2}+\frac{1}{\lambda_2^2}</math>

and the new skewness parameter ''&kappa;'' obeys:

:<math>\frac{\kappa^2-1}{\kappa\lambda}=\frac{\kappa_1^2-1}{\kappa_1\lambda_1}+\frac{\kappa_2^2-1}{\kappa_2\lambda_2}</math>

==Moments, mean, variance, skewness==

The ''n''-th moment of the ALD about ''m'' is given by
:<math>
E[(x-m)^n]=\frac{n!}{\lambda^n(\kappa+1/\kappa)}\,(\kappa^{-(n+1)}-(-\kappa)^{n+1})
</math>
From the [[binomial theorem]], the ''n''-th moment about zero (for ''m'' not zero) is then:
:<math>
E[x^n]=\frac{\lambda\,m^{n+1}}{\kappa+1/\kappa}\,\left(
 \sum_{i=0}^n\frac{n!}{(n-i)!}\,\frac{1}{(m\lambda\kappa)^{i+1}}
-\sum_{i=0}^n\frac{n!}{(n-i)!}\,\frac{1}{(-m\lambda/\kappa)^{i+1}}
\right)
</math>

:<math>=
\frac{ \lambda \, m^{n+1}}{\kappa+1/\kappa}
 \left(
e^{m \lambda\kappa} E_{-n}(m  \lambda\kappa )
-e^{-m \lambda/\kappa } E_{-n}(-m \lambda /\kappa)
\right)
</math>

where <math>E_n( )</math> is the generalized [[exponential integral]] function <math>E_n(x)=x^{n-1}\Gamma(1-n,x)</math>

The first moment about zero is the mean:

:<math>\mu=E[x]=m-\frac{\kappa-1/\kappa}{\lambda}</math>

The variance is:

:<math>\sigma^2=E[x^2]-\mu^2=\frac{1+\kappa^4}{\kappa^2\lambda^2}</math>

and the skewness is:

:<math>\frac{E[x^3]-3\mu\sigma^2-\mu^3}{\sigma^3}=\frac{2 \left(1-\kappa ^6\right)}{\left(\kappa ^4+1\right)^{3/2}}</math>

==Generating asymmetric Laplace variates==

Asymmetric Laplace variates (''X'') may be generated from a random variate ''U'' drawn from the uniform distribution in the interval (-&kappa;,1/&kappa;) by:

:<math>
X=m-\frac{1}{\lambda\,s\kappa^s}\log(1-U\,s\kappa^S)
</math>
where s=sgn(U).

They may also be generated as the difference of two [[exponential distribution]]s. If ''X<sub>1</sub>'' is drawn from exponential distribution with mean and rate (''m<sub>1</sub>'',&lambda;/&kappa;) and ''X<sub>2</sub>'' is drawn from an exponential distribution with mean and rate (''m<sub>2</sub>'',&lambda;&kappa;) then ''X<sub>1</sub>&nbsp;-&nbsp;X<sub>2</sub>'' is distributed according to the asymmetric Laplace distribution with parameters (''m1-m2'', &lambda;, &kappa;)

==Entropy==

The differential [[Entropy (information theory)|entropy]] of the ALD is

:<math>
H=-\int_{-\infty}^\infty f_{AL}(x)\log(f_{AL}(x)) dx = 1-\log\left(\frac{\lambda}{\kappa+1/\kappa}\right)
</math>

The ALD has the maximum entropy of all distributions with a fixed value (1/&lambda;) of <math>(x-m)\,s\kappa^s</math> where <math>s=\sgn(x-m)</math>.

==Alternative parametrization==

An alternative parametrization is made possible by the characteristic function:

<math>\varphi(t;\mu,\sigma,\beta)=\frac{ e^{i \mu t}}{1-i \beta \sigma t +\sigma^2 t^2}</math>

where <math>\mu</math>  is a [[location parameter]], <math>\sigma</math> is a [[scale parameter]], <math>\beta</math> is an [[asymmetry]] parameter. This is specified in Section 2.6.1 and Section 3.1 of Lihn (2015).
<ref name="LIHN2015">{{cite journal|last=Lihn|first=Stephen H.-T.|year=2015|title=The Special Elliptic Option Pricing Model and Volatility Smile|url=https://ssrn.com/abstract=2707810|journal=SSRN|page=2707810|access-date=2017-09-05}}</ref> Its [[probability density function]] is

:<math> f(x;\mu,\sigma,\beta)  = \frac{1}{2 \sigma B_0}
    \begin{cases}
      \exp \left( \frac{x-\mu}{\sigma B^-} \right) & \text{if }x < \mu
      \\[4pt]
      \exp ( -\frac{x-\mu}{\sigma B^+} )  & \text{if }x \geq \mu
    \end{cases}
  </math>

where <math>B_0=\sqrt{1+\beta^2/4}</math> and <math> B^\pm=B_0\pm\beta/2.</math> It follows that <math> B^+ B^- = 1, B^+ - B^- = \beta.</math>

The ''n''-th moment about <math>\mu</math>  is given by
:<math>
E[(x-\mu)^n]=\frac{\sigma^n n!}{2 B_0} ( (B^+)^{n+1} + (-1)^n (B^-)^{n+1} )
</math>
The mean about zero is:{{quote|<math> E[x]=\mu+\sigma \beta
  </math>}}The variance is:{{quote|<math> E[x^2]-E[x]^2=\sigma^2 (2+\beta^2)
  </math>}}The skewness is:{{quote|<math> \frac{2\beta (3+\beta^2)}{(2+\beta^2)^{3/2}}
  </math>}}The excess kurtosis is:{{quote|<math> \frac{6 (2+4\beta^2+\beta^4)}{(2+\beta^2)^{2}}
  </math>}}For small <math>\beta</math>, the skewness is about <math>3\beta/\sqrt{2}</math> . Thus <math>\beta</math> represents skewness in an almost direct way.

==Alternative parameterization for Bayesian quantile regression==
The Asymmetric Laplace distribution is commonly used with an alternative parameterization for performing [[quantile regression]] in a [[Bayesian inference]] context.<ref name=YUMO2001>{{cite journal|title=Bayesian quantile regression|last1=Yu |first1=Keming |last2=Moyeed |first2=Rana A. |page=437-447|year=2001|journal=Statistics & Probability Letters|volume=54|issue=4 |doi=10.1016/S0167-7152(01)00124-9 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0167715201001249|access-date=2022-01-09|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Under this approach, the <math>\kappa</math> parameter describing asymmetry is replaced with a <math>p</math> parameter indicating the percentile or quantile desired. Using this parameterization, the likelihood of the Asymmetric Laplace Distribution is equivalent to the loss function employed in [[quantile regression]]. With this alternative parameterization, the [[probability density function]] is defined as:

:<math> f(x;m,\lambda,p)  = \frac{p(1-p)}{\lambda}
    \begin{cases}
      \exp \left( -((p-1)/\lambda)(x-m) \right) & \text{if }x \leq m
      \\[4pt]
      \exp ( -(p/\lambda)(x-m) )  & \text{if }x > m
    \end{cases}
  </math>

Where, ''m'' is a [[location parameter]], ''&lambda;''&nbsp;>&nbsp;0 is a [[scale parameter]], and ''0&nbsp;<&nbsp;p&nbsp;<&nbsp;1'' is a [[percentile]] parameter. 

The mean (<math>\mu</math>) and variance (<math>\sigma^2</math>) are calculated as:

:<math>\mu=m+\frac{1-2p}{p(1-p)}\lambda</math>

:<math>\sigma^2=\frac{1-2p+2p^2}{p^2(1-p)^2}\lambda^2</math>

The [[cumulative distribution function]] is given<ref name=YUZH2005>{{cite journal|title=A Three-Parameter Asymmetric Laplace Distribution and Its Extension|last1=Yu |first1=Keming |last2=Zhang|first2=Jin |page=1867-1879|year=2005|journal=Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods|volume=34|issue=9–10 |doi=10.1080/03610920500199018 |s2cid=120827101 |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/03610920500199018|access-date=2022-01-30|url-access=subscription}}</ref> by:

:<math> F(x;m,\lambda,p)  = 
    \begin{cases}
      p\exp (\frac{1-p}{\lambda}(x-m)) & \text{if }x \leq m
      \\[4pt]
     1-(1-p) \exp (\frac{-p}{\lambda}(x-m))  & \text{if }x > m
    \end{cases}
  </math>
